This example shows how to generate distance/time matrices using the matrix API.


### Data 

```{r}

data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist.csv', stringsAsFactors = F)[1:6,]

number_pubs <- nrow(data)

```

The data used in this example is a list of `r number_pubs` pubs in Dublin, Ireland with their associated X and Y coordinates.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

if(!("pacman" %in% rownames(installed.packages()))){
  install.packages("pacman")
}

library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse)
p_load(DT)
p_load(dplyr)
```

```{r}

data <- data %>% mutate(across(2:3, ~ format(round(.x, digits=5), nsmall = 5))) 

datatable(data, colnames = c("Pub Name (id)",
                           "X-Coordinate (X)",
                           "Y-Coordinate (Y)")
                           , options = list(dom = 't', scrollY = "200px", pageLength=nrow(data), columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-right', targets = 2:3))))

```


### Running the example

An R script with all the lines needed to run the example can be found [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/examples/blob/master/R/matrix-2-intermediate.R).

The example uses the **iceR** package which will first need to be installed (see information [here](https://github.com/Icepack-co/iceR)) and then loaded.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(iceR)
```

|
Execute the example as follows:

1. Create an apiHelper object with the model type you'd like to solve

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'matrix-vyv95n7wchpl', configFile = '../config.json')
```


2. Create the model and add some data to it

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Create the model
model <- new (Matrix.MatrixRequest)

# Load the data
data <- read.csv('../sample_data/publist.csv', stringsAsFactors = F)[1:6,]

# Add the data to the model
model$locations <- apply(X = data,
                         MARGIN = 1,
                         FUN = function(i){
                           l <- new (Matrix.Location)
                           l$id <- i['id']
                           l$geocode$longitude <- as.numeric(i['X'])
                           l$geocode$latitude <- as.numeric(i['Y'])
                           return(l)
                         })

# create a 2x4 matrix. locations 1:2 to locations 3:6. Returns a total of 2*4 elements.
model$sources <- data$id[1:2]
model$destinations <- data$id[3:6]
model$distanceUnit <- 1
model$durationUnit <- 1

# View the model in plain-text format (string or JSON)
model$toString() %>% cat
model$toJSON() %>% cat

```

3. Submit the model to the API

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(model)  
```


4. Retrieve the model response

NOTE: It takes about a minute to solve
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
resp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)
```


5. Visualise the result

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Protobuf in string format
resp$toString() %>% cat  

# Tabulate the data in native-R format
tab <- resp %>% tabulate(model)
tab$elements %>% head # just inspect the head of the output
tab$elements %>% nrow 

# The response is tabulated in long form (i.e. "tidy").
# You might want it in matrix-form (or a wide-ish form). Just use reshape2 to do the heavy lifting here.
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| 
# Install reshape2 if not installed and then load
library("reshape2")
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true
#| 
tab$elements$fromId %>% unique
tab$elements$toId %>% unique
# NOTE: there is no overlap between the from's and to's based on the way we constructed the query.
tab$elements %>% reshape2::dcast(fromId ~ toId, value.var = 'distance', fill = 0) # distance matrix 
tab$elements %>% reshape2::dcast(fromId ~ toId, value.var = 'duration', fill = 0) # time matrix
# NOTE: if you leave the fill=0 off, you'll get NA's on the diagonal, which may or may not be what you want.

```
